candidates.title: New TAKT_FAKE_REVIEW_CALLS error branches are never exercised
candidates.detail: Review() now opens/writes/closes a calls-log file (lines 30-42) and returns an errorResult on any OpenFile, WriteString, or Close failure. No test in the wave (or elsewhere in the repo) drives any of these three failure modes — e.g. by pointing TAKT_FAKE_REVIEW_CALLS at an unwritable path or a directory. This is brand-new logic that other tests now depend on for correctness (oploop_test.go's TestSpecGateSpendsASecondScopedReviewOnABlockingRework and close_internal_test.go's TestBlindTaskReviewPromptNeverSeesTheLensClaims both rely on this file being written correctly to look up a call's exact LogID), so a silent regression in the write/error path (e.g. swallowing the error instead of returning it, or writing a malformed line) would go undetected.

candidates.title: singleQuoted duplicates the existing shellQuote escaping algorithm
candidates.detail: internal/cli/archive.go:353-355 already defines `shellQuote(s string) string { return "'" + strings.ReplaceAll(s, "'", `'\''`) + "'" }` for exactly this POSIX single-quote close-escape-reopen technique, with a comment explaining the same rationale repeated almost verbatim in the new singleQuoted's doc comment (internal/brief/brief.go:265-274). The new PRTitleQuoted (internal/brief/brief.go:275-281) reimplements the same one-line escaping rule in a different package instead of sharing it, so a future fix or hardening of the shell-escaping rule (e.g. for control characters) has two independent copies to update.

candidates.title: Body path interpolated unquoted in the same shell command whose title is carefully quoted
candidates.detail: `gh pr create --base {{.Base}} --title '{{.PRTitleQuoted}}' --body-file {{.PRBodyPath}}` quotes the title (via singleQuoted/PRTitleQuoted, added specifically because a shell would otherwise split the command on spaces) but leaves `--body-file {{.PRBodyPath}}` bare. PRBodyPath is finish.PRPath(bdir), an absolute path under the workspace/repo root, which can contain spaces just as much as any other filesystem path — the exact risk internal/cli/archive.go's shellQuote (used for discardSweep's `git clean -fd -- '<rel>'`) exists to guard against ('a worktree path is whatever the user's filesystem says — a space in it would otherwise split the command into arguments'). brief.go:279-280 asserts PRBodyPath is safe to interpolate bare 'since it is takt's own <bundle>/finish/pr.md', but that reasoning is exactly what shellQuote's own doc comment rejects for repo/bundle-relative paths. The same command should quote both arguments.

candidates.title: TAKT_FAKE_REVIEW_CALLS log-parsing loop duplicated across two test files
candidates.detail: internal/cli/oploop_test.go:881-891 and internal/cli/close_internal_test.go:324-333 (both added by this same task) contain near-identical logic: split the calls file on newlines, `strings.Cut` each line on the first space to get (rubric, logID), filter by rubric, then `strings.Cut` the matching line again to pull out the LogID for the logs/<id>.prompt read. A small shared helper (e.g. `callsForRubric(t, callsFile, rubric string) []string`) in the cli test package would avoid the two copies drifting (e.g. one trims trailing newline before splitting, the other doesn't need to since it reuses the same TrimRight call — but any future change to the calls-file format must be made in both places).

Searching the whole repository for TAKT_FAKE_REVIEW_CALLS usage in tests (oploop_test.go, close_internal_test.go) shows only the success path exercised — no test points TAKT_FAKE_REVIEW_CALLS at an unwritable path or directory to drive OpenFile/WriteString/Close failures.

internal/brief/brief.go:275 `func singleQuoted(s string) string { return strings.ReplaceAll(s, "'", `'\''`) }` duplicates the identical one-line escaping rule already defined in internal/cli/archive.go:353-355 `func shellQuote(s string) string { return "'" + strings.ReplaceAll(s, "'", `'\''`) + "'" }` (shellQuote just wraps the same ReplaceAll in outer quotes). Both comments independently explain the same close-escape-reopen POSIX technique. The two packages cannot share the helper without restructuring (cli already imports brief), but the core algorithm is genuinely duplicated in two places.

internal/brief/templates/run-push_pr.md:4 reads `gh pr create --base {{.Base}} --title '{{.PRTitleQuoted}}' --body-file {{.PRBodyPath}}` — the title is wrapped in single quotes with its apostrophes escaped, but PRBodyPath is interpolated bare. PRBodyPath = finish.PRPath(r.bdir), and r.bdir is built via bundle.Dir.Bundle(slug) = filepath.Join(repoRoot or externalBase, ..., slug) (internal/bundle/dir.go:59-64) — repoRoot is 'the absolute work-tree root', wherever the user's filesystem places it, with no validation against spaces or shell metacharacters (internal/bundle/paths.go's CheckRelPath and ValidSlug validate the slug and relative bundle dir, never the repo root). brief.go:279-280's own comment justifies the bare interpolation as safe 'since it is takt's own `<bundle>/finish/pr.md`', but only the trailing `finish/pr.md` segment is takt's own; the bundle-root prefix is the user's checkout path, exactly the class of value internal/cli/archive.go's shellQuote exists to guard ('a worktree path is whatever the user's filesystem says — a space in it would otherwise split the command into arguments').

internal/cli/oploop_test.go:880-893 and internal/cli/close_internal_test.go's TestBlindTaskReviewPromptNeverSeesTheLensClaims contain near-identical logic: `for line := range strings.SplitSeq(strings.TrimRight(string(callsRaw), "\n"), "\n") { if rubric, _, ok := strings.Cut(line, " "); ok && rubric == "<x>" { ... } }` followed by `strings.Cut` again to pull the LogID and read `filepath.Join(bdir, "logs", logID+".prompt")`. Both blocks were added in this same diff, and no shared helper factors the parsing out.
